bugs.title: No circular dependency detection in PipelineManager causes infinite wait
bugs.description: create_pipeline() inserts stages with arbitrary depends_on lists without validating the dependency graph is a DAG. If stages form a cycle (A->B->C->A), all cycled stages remain in 'waiting' forever because none of their dependencies can ever complete. The pipeline is permanently stalled with no error or warning.
bugs.reproduction: pm.create_pipeline('cycle', [{'name': 'A', 'depends_on': ['B']}, {'name': 'B', 'depends_on': ['C']}, {'name': 'C', 'depends_on': ['A']}]). All stages stay 'waiting'. get_ready_stages() returns empty list forever.
bugs.impact: Silent permanent pipeline stall. No way to detect or recover. The pipeline appears 'active' but can never complete.
bugs.test_needed: Test that create_pipeline raises ValueError when given stages with a cycle (A->B->C->A). Test that valid DAGs still work. Test self-dependency (A depends on A).

bugs.title: complete_work does not verify the claimer matches the caller
bugs.description: complete_work(work_id, result) updates the work item unconditionally with UPDATE ... WHERE id = ?. It does not check that self.team matches claimed_by. Any team can mark any other team's claimed work as completed with arbitrary result data, corrupting the coordination protocol.
bugs.reproduction: ws_a.enqueue_work('task'); ws_a.steal_work()  # claimed by team-a. ws_b = WorkStealing(..., team='team-b', ...); ws_b.complete_work(1, {'fake': 'result'})  # succeeds, should not.
bugs.impact: Work items completed with incorrect results. Silent data corruption. No audit trail integrity.
bugs.test_needed: Test that team-b cannot complete_work on an item claimed by team-a (raises PermissionError). Test that completing unclaimed or nonexistent items raises ValueError.

bugs.title: Abandoned claimed work items never return to queue (zombie work)
bugs.description: When a team calls steal_work() claiming an item, then crashes without calling complete_work() or fail_work(), the item remains in 'claimed' status forever. No timeout mechanism exists despite claimed_at being recorded. The item is invisible to steal_work() (which filters status='queued') and can never be processed by another team.
bugs.reproduction: ws.enqueue_work('task'); ws.steal_work()  # claimed_at recorded. # Team crashes / never calls complete or fail. # Item stuck as 'claimed' forever. ws2.steal_work()  # returns None even though work exists.
bugs.impact: Work items permanently lost to the system. Silent data loss in coordination. Over time, abandoned items accumulate and work never gets done.
bugs.fix:
Add a recover_abandoned method to WorkStealing and optionally call it from steal_work:

    @_retry_on_busy
    def recover_abandoned(self, timeout_seconds: float = 1800) -> int:
        """Re-queue work items claimed longer than timeout_seconds ago.

        Returns the number of items recovered.
        """
        cutoff = time.time() - timeout_seconds
        with self._lock:
            cur = self._conn.execute(
                """UPDATE work_queue
                   SET status = 'queued', claimed_by = NULL, claimed_at = NULL
                   WHERE status = 'claimed' AND claimed_at < ?""",
                (cutoff,),
            )
            count = cur.rowcount
            self._conn.commit()
        if count > 0:
            logger.info("Recovered %d abandoned work items (timeout=%ds)", count, timeout_seconds)
        return count
bugs.test_needed: Test that a claimed item older than the timeout gets re-queued by recover_abandoned. Test that recently claimed items are not recovered. Test that recovered items can be stolen again.

bugs.title: No stage failure/retry handling in pipelines
bugs.description: Pipeline stages have no 'failed' status. The code explicitly acknowledges this: 'any_failed = False  # no failure state for stages currently' (line 513). If a stage encounters an error, there is no way to mark it failed, no retry mechanism, and downstream stages are blocked forever. The only options are to leave it in_progress (zombie) or mark it completed with error data (corrupts the data model).
bugs.reproduction: Create a pipeline A->B->C. Start stage A. Stage A encounters an error. No fail_stage() method exists. Stage A stays in_progress. B and C never become ready.
bugs.impact: Any stage failure permanently stalls the pipeline. Teams must hack around this by completing with error data, destroying result integrity.
bugs.fix:
Add fail_stage method and update get_pipeline_status to detect failures:

    @_retry_on_busy
    def fail_stage(self, pipeline_id: int, stage_name: str, error: str, retry: bool = False) -> None:
        """Mark a stage as failed. If retry=True, reset to 'ready' instead."""
        now = time.time()
        with self._lock:
            if retry:
                self._conn.execute(
                    """UPDATE pipeline_stages
                       SET status = 'ready', started_at = NULL
                       WHERE pipeline_id = ? AND stage_name = ?""",
                    (pipeline_id, stage_name),
                )
            else:
                self._conn.execute(
                    """UPDATE pipeline_stages
                       SET status = 'failed', output_data = ?, completed_at = ?
                       WHERE pipeline_id = ? AND stage_name = ?""",
                    (json.dumps({"error": error}), now, pipeline_id, stage_name),
                )
            self._conn.commit()

        _bus_notify(self.bus_dir, "global", self.agent_id, self.team, {
            "event": "pipeline-stage-failed" if not retry else "pipeline-stage-retrying",
            "pipeline_id": pipeline_id,
            "stage_name": stage_name,
            "error": error,
        })

Also update get_pipeline_status (line 512-513):
        any_failed = any(s["status"] == "failed" for s in stages)
        status_val = "completed" if all_completed else ("failed" if any_failed else pipeline_row["status"])
bugs.test_needed: Test fail_stage marks stage as 'failed'. Test retry=True resets to 'ready'. Test pipeline status shows 'failed' when any stage fails. Test downstream stages remain 'waiting' when upstream fails.

bugs.title: Duplicate stage names accepted silently in create_pipeline
bugs.description: create_pipeline does not validate stage name uniqueness within a pipeline. If two stages share the same name, SQL queries using WHERE pipeline_id = ? AND stage_name = ? (used in start_stage, complete_stage, check_stage_ready) match both rows, causing UPDATE to modify both. depends_on references become ambiguous. trigger_downstream may double-trigger.
bugs.reproduction: pm.create_pipeline('dup', [{'name': 'step', 'team': 'a'}, {'name': 'step', 'team': 'b', 'depends_on': ['step']}]). Two rows inserted with stage_name='step'. start_stage(pid, 'step') updates both rows.
bugs.impact: Undefined behavior: both duplicate stages get started/completed simultaneously. Dependency resolution breaks. Pipeline state becomes inconsistent.
bugs.fix:
Add validation at the start of create_pipeline, before the database insert:

        now = time.time()
        # Validate stage name uniqueness
        stage_names = [s["name"] for s in stages]
        if len(stage_names) != len(set(stage_names)):
            dupes = [n for n in stage_names if stage_names.count(n) > 1]
            raise ValueError(f"Duplicate stage names: {set(dupes)}")
        with self._lock:
bugs.test_needed: Test that create_pipeline raises ValueError when two stages share the same name.

bugs.title: No double-start guard for pipeline stages
bugs.description: start_stage() does UPDATE SET status='in_progress' without checking the current status. A stage that is already 'in_progress' can be started again (resetting started_at). Worse, a 'completed' stage can be reverted to 'in_progress', causing pipeline regression. The UPDATE has no WHERE status='ready' guard.
bugs.reproduction: pm.start_stage(pid, 'step1'); pm.complete_stage(pid, 'step1', {}). pm.start_stage(pid, 'step1')  # re-starts a completed stage!
bugs.impact: Completed stages can be reverted, breaking pipeline progress. started_at timestamps become unreliable. Downstream stages that already triggered may produce duplicate work.
bugs.fix:
Add a status guard to start_stage:

    @_retry_on_busy
    def start_stage(self, pipeline_id: int, stage_name: str) -> None:
        """Mark a stage as in_progress. Only allowed if status is 'ready'."""
        now = time.time()
        with self._lock:
            cur = self._conn.execute(
                """UPDATE pipeline_stages SET status = 'in_progress', started_at = ?
                   WHERE pipeline_id = ? AND stage_name = ? AND status = 'ready'""",
                (now, pipeline_id, stage_name),
            )
            if cur.rowcount == 0:
                row = self._conn.execute(
                    "SELECT status FROM pipeline_stages WHERE pipeline_id = ? AND stage_name = ?",
                    (pipeline_id, stage_name),
                ).fetchone()
                status = row["status"] if row else "not found"
                self._conn.commit()
                raise ValueError(
                    f"Cannot start stage '{stage_name}': current status is '{status}' (must be 'ready')"
                )
            self._conn.commit()

        _bus_notify(self.bus_dir, "global", self.agent_id, self.team, {
            "event": "pipeline-stage-started",
            "pipeline_id": pipeline_id,
            "stage_name": stage_name,
        })
bugs.test_needed: Test that starting a 'completed' stage raises ValueError. Test that starting an 'in_progress' stage raises ValueError. Test that starting a 'waiting' stage raises ValueError. Test normal 'ready' -> 'in_progress' still works.

bugs.title: Bus notification failures crash callers
bugs.description: _bus_notify uses os.open/os.write for atomic JSONL append but has no exception handling around the file I/O. If the bus directory is deleted, disk is full, or permissions change, os.open or os.write raises OSError. This exception propagates up through enqueue_work, steal_work, complete_work, etc., crashing the caller AFTER the SQLite transaction has already committed. The state change is persisted but the caller sees an error.
bugs.reproduction: ws = WorkStealing(db_path, '/nonexistent/path/that/gets/deleted', 'team', 'agent'). os.rmdir(bus_dir) after initialization. ws.enqueue_work('task')  # SQLite insert succeeds, then _bus_notify crashes with OSError.
bugs.impact: Caller gets an exception even though the database operation succeeded. State and notifications diverge. In retry scenarios, the caller may retry the database operation causing duplicates.
bugs.fix:
Wrap the file I/O in _bus_notify with try/except:

def _bus_notify(bus_dir: str, channel: str, agent_id: str, team: str, body: dict) -> None:
    """Fire-and-forget bus notification (JSONL atomic append)."""
    if bus_dir is None:
        return
    try:
        os.makedirs(bus_dir, exist_ok=True)
        msg = {
            "id": str(uuid.uuid4()),
            "type": "info",
            "channel": channel,
            "team": team,
            "agent_id": agent_id,
            "ts": time.time(),
            "ttl": 3600,
            "body": body,
        }
        raw = json.dumps(msg, separators=(",", ":")).encode("utf-8") + b"\n"
        safe_ch = channel.replace("/", "_").replace("..", "_")
        filepath = os.path.join(bus_dir, f"{safe_ch}.jsonl")
        fd = os.open(filepath, os.O_WRONLY | os.O_APPEND | os.O_CREAT, 0o644)
        try:
            os.write(fd, raw)
        finally:
            os.close(fd)
    except OSError as e:
        logger.warning("Bus notification failed (channel=%s): %s", channel, e)
bugs.test_needed: Test that enqueue_work succeeds even when bus_dir is invalid/deleted. Test that a warning is logged but no exception propagates.

bugs.title: Scratchpad cleanup_expired has no automatic scheduling
bugs.description: cleanup_expired() only runs when explicitly called. No part of the system triggers it automatically. Expired entries accumulate on disk indefinitely. The read/read_all methods filter by expires_at so expired entries are invisible but still consume storage. Over extended operation, the scratchpad table grows without bound.
bugs.reproduction: Write 100,000 entries with TTL=1. Wait 2 seconds. All entries expired but still on disk. Database file stays large. Only manual cleanup_expired() reclaims space.
bugs.impact: Unbounded database growth. Degraded query performance as table grows. Eventual disk exhaustion in long-running systems.
bugs.fix:
Add a write counter and auto-cleanup trigger to the Scratchpad class:

    def __init__(self, db_path: str, team: str, agent_id: str, auto_cleanup_interval: int = 100) -> None:
        self.db_path = db_path
        self.team = team
        self.agent_id = agent_id
        self._lock = threading.Lock()
        self._conn = _open_db(db_path)
        self._write_count = 0
        self._auto_cleanup_interval = auto_cleanup_interval

    @_retry_on_busy
    def write(self, key: str, value: Any, namespace: Optional[str] = None, ttl: int = 3600) -> None:
        """Write a key-value pair. Overwrites if key+namespace already exists."""
        ns = namespace or self.team
        now = time.time()
        expires_at = now + ttl
        with self._lock:
            self._conn.execute(
                """INSERT INTO scratchpad (key, namespace, value, written_by, ttl_seconds, created_at, expires_at)
                   VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)
                   ON CONFLICT(key, namespace) DO UPDATE SET
                       value=excluded.value, written_by=excluded.written_by,
                       ttl_seconds=excluded.ttl_seconds, created_at=excluded.created_at,
                       expires_at=excluded.expires_at""",
                (key, ns, json.dumps(value), self.agent_id, ttl, now, expires_at),
            )
            self._conn.commit()
            self._write_count += 1
            if self._write_count >= self._auto_cleanup_interval:
                self._write_count = 0
                self._conn.execute("DELETE FROM scratchpad WHERE expires_at <= ?", (now,))
                self._conn.commit()
bugs.test_needed: Test that after auto_cleanup_interval writes, expired entries are automatically deleted. Test that non-expired entries are not affected.

bugs.title: TOCTOU race in get_ready_stages: check and update not atomic
bugs.description: get_ready_stages() reads all stages under the lock (line 468-472), releases the lock, computes which are ready (line 474-481), then re-acquires the lock to update statuses (line 484-491). Between the read and the update, another thread can call start_stage() changing a stage from 'waiting' to 'in_progress'. The update then overwrites it back to 'ready' because it uses UPDATE SET status='ready' WHERE id=? without checking current status.
bugs.reproduction: Thread 1: get_ready_stages() reads stages, finds stage X is 'waiting' with deps met. Thread 2: start_stage(pid, 'X') sets X to 'in_progress'. Thread 1: updates X to 'ready', reverting the start.
bugs.impact: A stage that was started gets reverted to 'ready'. Team that started it thinks it's running; the database says it's ready. Another team may also start it, causing duplicate execution.
bugs.test_needed: Test concurrent get_ready_stages and start_stage: start_stage should not be reverted. Verify with a barrier-synchronized test where one thread calls get_ready_stages while another calls start_stage on the same pipeline.

bugs.title: No database indexes on frequently queried columns
bugs.description: The schema has no secondary indexes. steal_work() does a full table scan with WHERE status='queued' ORDER BY priority ASC, created_at ASC. get_ready_stages() and trigger_downstream() scan pipeline_stages by pipeline_id. Scratchpad reads scan by namespace + expires_at. At scale (10K+ rows), these become significant performance bottlenecks.
bugs.reproduction: Insert 100,000 work items. Call steal_work() repeatedly. Each call scans the entire table to find status='queued' items. Similarly, create 1,000 pipelines with 100 stages each, then query get_ready_stages on the latest pipeline.
bugs.impact: Linear query degradation with table size. steal_work() latency increases from <1ms to 100ms+ at 100K rows. Pipeline queries suffer similarly.
bugs.test_needed: Performance test: insert 10K work items, measure steal_work latency with and without indexes. Should be <10ms with indexes. Similarly test pipeline queries with 100K stage rows.

bugs.title: TOCTOU race in trigger_downstream: read and update not atomic
bugs.description: trigger_downstream() has the same pattern as get_ready_stages: reads all stages under lock (line 529-533), releases lock, computes newly ready stages (line 535-543), re-acquires lock to update (line 546-552). Between the read and update, concurrent trigger_downstream calls from other threads completing different stages can cause the same stage to be marked 'ready' twice, or a status to be overwritten. The stress test test_concurrent_stage_completions (line 487) expects sink to appear exactly once, but the TOCTOU window means it could appear 0 or 2 times.
bugs.reproduction: Fan-in pipeline: 5 sources -> 1 sink. Complete all 5 sources concurrently. Each calls trigger_downstream. Two threads read all stages while source-4 and source-5 are both completing. Both compute sink as newly ready. Both update sink to 'ready'. Sink appears in both return values.
bugs.impact: Downstream stage triggered multiple times causing duplicate work. The existing stress test (test_concurrent_stage_completions) actually tests for this and may flake.
bugs.fix:
Use an atomic conditional UPDATE to prevent double-trigger:

        # Update status to ready (only if still 'waiting' to prevent double-trigger)
        with self._lock:
            actually_ready: list[str] = []
            for name in newly_ready:
                cur = self._conn.execute(
                    "UPDATE pipeline_stages SET status = 'ready' WHERE pipeline_id = ? AND stage_name = ? AND status = 'waiting'",
                    (pipeline_id, name),
                )
                if cur.rowcount > 0:
                    actually_ready.append(name)
            self._conn.commit()

        # Bus notification for each actually-ready stage
        for name in actually_ready:
            _bus_notify(self.bus_dir, "global", self.agent_id, self.team, {
                "event": "pipeline-stage-ready",
                "pipeline_id": pipeline_id,
                "stage_name": name,
                "triggered_by": completed_stage,
            })

        return actually_ready
bugs.test_needed: Stress test: 10 sources -> 1 sink, complete all 10 concurrently, verify sink appears exactly once across all trigger_downstream return values. Run 100 iterations to catch races.

bugs.title: fail_work does not verify the claimer matches the caller
bugs.description: Same issue as complete_work (BUG-WS-002): fail_work() updates the work item unconditionally. Any team can fail any other team's claimed work without authorization. Additionally, fail_work can be called on items in any status (queued, completed, etc.), not just claimed items.
bugs.reproduction: ws_a.steal_work()  # team-a claims item. ws_b.fail_work(1, 'sabotage')  # team-b fails team-a's work. Also: ws.fail_work(999, 'reason')  # fails a nonexistent item (silent no-op).
bugs.impact: Work items failed by unauthorized teams. No audit integrity. Silent no-ops when called with invalid IDs hide bugs.
bugs.test_needed: Test that team-b cannot fail_work on team-a's claimed item. Test that failing an unclaimed item raises ValueError.

bugs.title: check_stage_ready acquires lock twice in non-atomic pattern
bugs.description: check_stage_ready() acquires self._lock to read depends_on (line 405-409), releases it, then re-acquires it to check each dependency's status (line 418-425). Between these two lock acquisitions, another thread could complete or reset stages, making the result stale. Additionally, the second locked section queries dependencies one at a time in a loop, holding the lock for N queries where N is the number of dependencies.
bugs.reproduction: Thread 1 calls check_stage_ready for stage C (depends on A, B). It reads deps=[A,B], releases lock. Thread 2 completes A. Thread 1 re-acquires lock, sees A completed, B completed -> returns True. But if Thread 2 had reset B between the two lock acquisitions, Thread 1 would return incorrect True.
bugs.impact: Minor: check_stage_ready could return a stale result. Low impact since callers should use get_ready_stages or trigger_downstream for actual state changes.
bugs.test_needed: Existing tests for check_stage_ready should still pass. Add a concurrent test: one thread completes a stage while another calls check_stage_ready.
